method: Read primary EC3 annotation dictionaries with pikepdf (Subj, Subtype, NM, IRT/NM, QuadPoints, Rect, Contents), rendered pages, and page text/bounding boxes. Compared effective targets with current audit statements. Page references below give physical PDF page and printed footer.

coverage.scope_limit: Nine linked replacement pairs across six issues, plus selected #474 insertion. The additional unlinked #292 deletion is distinct. Not a complete issue/EC3 inventory.

annotation_evidence.target: The strike quad overlays the word 'should' in 'the Length entry should still specify the number of those bytes'; the caret supplies 'shall'.

findings.effective_change: The Length-entry sentence now says it shall still specify the number of bytes. The separate preceding sentence that embedded stream bytes shall be ignored when /F is present is not crossed out and is not the target of this replacement.

current_audit_claims.claim: Historical draft attributed #10 to the adjacent ignore-bytes sentence.
current_audit_claims.verdict: Previously corrected/promoted as checkpoint114 finding D66. This sample verifies the primary target only; do not count it as a new current finding.

current_audit_claims.claim: Historical draft linked a reader-refusal test directly to #10.
current_audit_claims.verdict: Checkpoint114 parent review explicitly corrected this. The current parent-reviewed artifact now treats the test as the distinct /F reader path, not evidence for the Length edit. No outstanding current mismatch is claimed.

findings.verdict: Primary geometry independently verifies the corrected D66 disposition from checkpoint114; no duplicate/open finding.

replacement_1.target: On physical 49, replaces “are” in the sentence requiring the filter choices to be specified in the stream dictionary.

replacement_2.target: On physical 50, the strike covers “files” in “PDF files support a standard set of filters”; replacement inserts “processors shall”, yielding the reader obligation that processors shall support the standard filter set.

findings.effective_change: Issue #216 has two distinct source effects across physical 49–50: a producer-side requirement to specify filter choices in the stream dictionary, and a reader-side requirement for processors to support the standard filter set. The second target is relevant to Table 6 support tests.

current_audit_claims.claim: #216 on physical pp. 49–50 changes §7.4.1 filter-language obligations and supports existing Table 6 support tests.
current_audit_claims.verdict: CORRECT AT THIS SCOPE: the p49 edit targets dictionary specification; the p50 edit replaces “files” with “processors shall” in the standard-filter support sentence. The Table 6 test link is supported by p50. Do not reduce #216 to only the p49 edit.

findings.verdict: Previously alleged wrong-evidence link withdrawn. Full two-page issue overlay supports both writer- and reader-side changes and current filter-test attribution.

findings.source_location: EC3 physical 157 / printed 142; Table 49 URL row

annotation_evidence.target: The strike covers the Table 49 URL-row parenthetical beginning '(Optional; PDF 2.0; shall be a direct object if present)'; the replacement label is Required.

findings.separate_annotation: A distinct Caret on the same page says the URL assigned by a developer should be unique for each extension; it is not the Table 49 replacement target.
findings.current_audit_claim: compatibility_extensions_current correctly identifies URL as required by #732 and keeps unique-URL guidance separate.
findings.verdict: Target attribution verified. Preserve the source tension with §7.12.6's surviving 'optional URL' prose as a separate interpretive issue; the geometry does not resolve that tension.

replacement_1.target: The strike quad overlays 'shall' in 'they shall be ordered over time'; replacement makes the clause 'they should be ordered over time'.

replacement_2.target: Two strike quads cover 'shall be a monotonically increasing sequence'; replacement produces 'numbers should increase over time'.

current_audit_claims.claim: #239 changes the monotonic ExtensionLevel-over-time wording to a recommendation.
current_audit_claims.verdict: CORRECT BUT INCOMPLETE if read as a complete account: there are two replacement locations in the same §7.12.5 sentence, and both shall statements become should statements.

current_audit_claims.claim: #239 replaces shall with should in the ExtensionLevel increase-over-time sentence.
current_audit_claims.verdict: CORRECT FOR THE SECOND TARGET; it omits the separate 'they shall be ordered' to 'they should be ordered' edit. No opposing substantive claim found.

findings.verdict: Both source replacements are real and aligned in effect. Existing narrow summaries are not false, but should not be treated as an exhaustive annotation inventory.

findings.source_location: EC3 physical 287 / printed 272; §8.10.2 and Table 93 Resources cell

replacement_1.caret_contents: it is strongly recommended that form XObjects be independent of the content streams in which they appear; from PDF 2.0 this is required
replacement_1.target: The linked multi-line strike covers the prior independent-resource text; replacement sets strong recommendation generally and requirement starting PDF 2.0.

replacement_2.target: The strike covers the Table 93 Resources-cell phrase 'Optional but strongly recommended'; replacement is 'Sometimes required'.

findings.current_audit_claim: form_xobject_cells_current identifies both version-conditioned independence wording and Table 93 Resources cell change.
findings.verdict: Target mapping verified. Keep the PDF 1.2+/pre-2.0 recommendation and PDF 2.0 requirement distinct; no reader-side rejection follows solely from the producer constraint.

findings.source_location: EC3 physical 395 / printed 380; Table 132 Type 5 halftone Default row

caret.contents: The halftone shall not be a Type 5 halftone.

annotation_evidence.target: The overlay changes the Type 5 halftone Default row's struck 'The value shall not be 5' text to the sentence in Contents.

findings.current_audit_claim: halftones_separations_current accurately treats #12 as a producer/table entry clarification, distinct from #311's deletion of the Type 5 contrast paragraph.
findings.verdict: Target and scope verified; do not conflate with #311.

additional_insertion_checked.source_location: EC3 physical 359 / printed 344; Table 120 FontWeight row
additional_insertion_checked.annotation: A Caret (NM 68e86e6a-6eb7-43a2-8d4a94648edd0ff5; no StrikeOut/IRT) inserts 'be between 1 and 1000 inclusive, and should' in the FontWeight sentence. Rendered caret is adjacent to the FontWeight value wording, not Descent despite the low-y annotation rectangle coordinate.
additional_insertion_checked.effective_reading: The permitted weight range is 1–1000 (SHALL); using the canonical hundred values 100–900 is SHOULD. This matches font_descriptor_cells_current. It is an insertion, not a replacement pair, and confirms why issue geometry must be checked against page orientation and actual body text.

unreviewed: Other errata issues and all unlisted Caret/StrikeOut groups
